dedupe_keys.name: national agriculture imagery program naip 1 m aerial orthoimagery 2003 to present usda fsa distributed by usgs eros

description: Leaf-on aerial orthoimagery of the United States at 1 metre ground sample distance, acquired during the agricultural growing season. The USGS DataCite record says the programme is run by the USDA Farm Service Agency through the Aerial Photography Field Office in Salt Lake City, began in 2003 on a 5-year cycle and moved to a 3-year cycle in 2009, with contracts let each year according to funding. Tiles are 3.75-minute quarter quadrangles with a 300 m buffer, in natural colour or colour near-infrared (four bands), with up to 10 percent cloud cover per tile. USGS EROS distributes the tiles as downloadable GeoTIFF and JPEG2000 files, the latter with 10:1 lossy compression; quarter quads use UTM on NAD83, while JPEG2000 files after 2013 use Web Mercator on WGS84. The record carries a CC0 1.0 dedication and has been updated since 2003. Since 2006 the specification requires well-defined points to lie within 6 m of true ground at 95 percent confidence. Coverage is the conterminous United States, state by state. Caveats: acquisition years differ by state, and lossy compression slightly degrades JPEG2000 imagery. For simulation it is a base layer to digitise farm buildings, grain storage, irrigation pivots, rural roads and utility corridors, and to map exposure after floods or storms. A related catalogue record is the USDA Cropland Data Layer.
